To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the supramolecular ordering of the p-terphenyldicarbonitrile molecules is driven by substrate templating and lateral interactions, (ii) chiral resolution occurs during the 2-D self-assembly process and (iii) the supramolecules are stabilized by attractive and directional interactions, which can be switched on and off at will.

the non-linear prochiral molecule p-terphenyldicarbonitrile adsorption on the Ag(1 1 1) surface results in the formation of large supramolecular islands with three stereoisomers (trans-1 and trans-2, cis) and a chiral resolution at low temperature.

the supramolecular organization of the non-linear molecule [1,1';4', 1'']- terphenyl-3,3"-dicarbonitri le on the Ag(1 11) surface is driven by a substrate templating and a chiral resolution mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self-assembly of a non-linear, pro-chiral molecule at a metal surface, whereby the supramolecular organization of the adsorbate is controlled by the operation of non-covalent interactions.
the supramolecular organization of a prochiral molecule on a metal surface and the chiral resolution of the molecule upon 2D confinement.
the supramolecular self-assembly and chiral resolution processes of the non-linear p-terphenylene derivative on the Ag( 111) surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chiral resolution of the trans-species is a consequence of the substrate templating effect and the molecular chirality.
chiral resolution of the trans-species during the 2 D self-assembly process on Ag(111) is driven by the operation of weak, noncovalent lateral forces.

the supramolecular organization of the adsorbate is determined by a complex interplay of the molecular geometry, the substrate templating effect and the operation of lateral interactions, which can be tuned in a well-defined fashion by the temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chiral resolution is a consequence of the molecular packing scheme and that the chirality of the molecules is not a prerequisite for chiral resolution.
the chirality of a prochiral molecule is induced by the substrate, the chiral recognition of the substrate and the chiral resolution of the supramolecular self-assembly process.
the supramolecular organization of p-ter-phenyl-m-dimethylamino-m-dicarbononitrile on the surface of Ag(111) can be used as a template for chiral resolution of the molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chiral resolution of a prochiral molecule is a general phenomenon in supramolecular 2D self-assembly on metal surfaces.
the chiral resolution is not a result of the formation of a chiral supramolecular structure.
the chirality of the molecules is expressed by the supramolecular organization of the molecules in the solid state.
